svg.title: From capability sets to concrete calls
svg.desc: A conceptual map separates registration, entry-point availability, model visibility, model proposals or code routing, and concrete execution decisions. Each point requires different evidence. The diagram does not claim that both projects share a complete pipeline.
svg.text: From capability sets to concrete calls
Reading the architecture: one module may handle several points, and Context changes may trigger recomposition.

g.text: 1 Registered
Capability definitions in the Registry
Evidence: source, name, version
2 Available at entry
By Agent, mode, and loading conditions
Evidence: filters and resulting list
3 Visible to the model
Descriptions in this actual request
Evidence: request tool Schemas

svg.text: Code can route directly, without model exposure

g.text: 4-B Code selects the call
Select tools and arguments via input, rules, or code.
Evidence: selected route and extraction result.
A tool may execute without a model Tool Call.
4-A Model proposes the call
Return a tool name, arguments, and call identity.
Evidence: actual Provider response and decoded result.
A direct answer may contain no tool call.

g.data-node: 5 Verify the execution decision for this call
g.text: 5 Verify the execution decision for this call
Check the actual consumer, trusted identity, resources, policy, and approval.
Evidence: allowed, denied, pending confirmation, or unavailable.
Concrete checks depend on the product and execution path.

svg.text: Schema validation checks input shape; resource access still requires checking the authorization consumer for the concrete call.
This map identifies observation points; it does not claim that CCB and Chat Gun implement the same five-stage pipeline.
Previously exposed descriptions do not vanish when hidden later; current conditions still need checking at execution.
Conceptual diagram · Based on the pinned CCB / Chat Gun versions in the article · Not an execution sequence record
